title: Limits of personal and home policies

sections.skill: Recognize where personal and home policies stop covering business use

questions.prompt: Does a homeowners policy always cover a home business?

choices.text: Yes, but only if the business is profitable
Not necessarily; coverage may be limited or excluded
No home policy can ever be changed
Yes, every home policy covers any business fully

questions.correct_answer: Not necessarily; coverage may be limited or excluded
questions.intro: Many owners assume their HOMEOWNERS or RENTERS insurance covers a home business. Often it does not, or covers very little: business equipment and inventory may have low limits, and injuries to customers visiting the home for business may be excluded. A PERSONAL AUTO policy may not cover driving for business deliveries. Ask your insurer directly: "Does this policy cover my business activities?" Options can include a home-business add-on (often called an endorsement) or a separate business policy.

sections.skill: A family car used as a taxi

questions.prompt: Why might the car insurer refuse a taxi claim?

choices.text: Business driving was not part of the policy
The trip was too short to count as driving

questions.correct_answer: Business driving was not part of the policy
questions.intro: Imagine using the family car to drive paying passengers. The family car insurance was priced for school runs and grocery trips, not for business driving all day. The insurer may say the business use was never part of the deal. Home and personal policies work the same way: they were priced for personal life, so business activities may fall outside them.
